newsitem.title: SPAIN: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV OUT AS BARCELONA SEEDS TUMBLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV OUT AS BARCELONA SEEDS TUMBLE.

text.p: Just six of the 16 seeds were left in the Barcelona Open as French Open champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov became the latest leading player to crash out on Wednesday.

However, local favourite Carlos Moya did buck the trend to avenge a recent defeat by compatriot Francisco Clavet and is on course to meet title holder Thomas Muster in a repeat of last year's semifinal.
Second seed Kafelnikov was beset by unforced errors and lost his way against Sweden's Magnus Larsson, who won the second round tie 3-6 6-2 6-3.

Last year's beaten finalist, fifth seed Marcelo Rios of Chile, was unable to cope with the tremendous power of unheralded Spaniard Alberto Portas, who came back from 4-1 down and saved three set points to take the first set 7-5.
The world number nine was at times outmanouevered by Portas, who has slipped to 133 in the rankings after missing much of last season with a knee injury.
Portas took the second set 7-6, Rios' resistance effectively ending when he netted an easy forehand put-away at 2-2 in the tie-break.
"In the tie-break I was right at the limit, to be honest. I don't know quite what happened, if he played badly, or if he was uncomfortable with my play," said Portas.
Portas faces another unfancied Spaniard, Fernando Vicente, in the next round, with a quarter-final place at stake against either Christian Ruud or Karim Alami, both unseeded.
Moya, seeded fourth, will face Morocco's Hicham Arazi after beating Clavet 6-4 6-4 just a week after falling to his compatriot in Estoril.
The Australian Open finalist recovered his clay court form after an uncharacteristic slip in Portugal.
"I don't know what happened to me last week ... I've been doing morning and afternoon training sessions since then," said Moya, who acknowledged having fitness problems.
Clavet, the losing finalist in Estoril, failed to take his only opportunity after breaking Moya early in the second set.
The Spanish number one took consecutive breaks after eliminating his backhand errors and mixing some outstanding lobs and drop shots into his baseline game.
"I'm pleased not for the result, but for the way I played," said Moya, who added his confidence had been affected by the defeat in Estoril and Spain's surprise Davis Cup elimination by Italy.
"Since the Australian Open, I've only really felt good in one game, and I lost some fitness on the American Tour," he said.
The most significant obstacle in Moya's path to the semifinals could be Andrei Medvedev.
The Ukranian followed Tuesday's victory over Estoril winner Alex Corretja with a comprehensive 6-2 6-0 win over another Spaniard, Carlos Costa.
